Subject: Notice: onboarding Protean Data as downstream partner (Order Form amendment)

Hi Markus,

Per our procurement workflow, Orbital is planning to onboard a downstream partner (Protean Data LLC) to provide log enrichment and transient storage for the new Edge Observability bundle tied to Order Form #ORD-2026-1101. This is a subprocessor addition that will be within the scope of the OF: they will receive ephemeral request/response logs (no raw customer files) and will be covered by a DPA annex.

Attached: vendor_subprocessor_list.csv (list + scopes), protean_dpa_draft.pdf (vendor-provided annex).

Two asks:
- Please confirm Redwood approval path for adding a subcontractor to an existing OF — specifically whether we need a full MSA redline or an OF-only amendment.
- If there are any open legal/security concerns in the draft DPA, let us know the minimal remediation items to keep the onboarding on the week-of-Nov 15 workback.

Timeline: Protean expects to be added to the environment on or before Nov 22; Orbital needs doc execution by Nov 15 to meet internal change freeze.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Alec Turner

Thanks Alec — looping in Jordan (ops) and Kim (legal). A few quick items from product/ops perspective:

- Scope confirmation: is Protean accessing any customer PII? You flagged ephemeral logs; if anything containing identifiers will be retained >30 days we need an S3 residency exception.
- Encryption: confirm at-rest encryption keys (vendor-managed vs customer-managed).
- Minimal contract ask from our side: a limited OF amendment that references a DPA Annex should be sufficient provided the DPA annex contains the right flow-downs (data access, audit rights, subprocessors, deletion obligations).

I attached a brief proposed redline for the OF/MSA that covers the flow-down language we typically require — markus_proposed_redline_msa.docx. Kimberly: please review DPA draft and call out any non-negotiable language; if this is a full MSA redline we should say so now.

If we can resolve the DPA redlines by Nov 10, I think we can meet Orbital's November 15 doc execution request.

Markus

Subject: Re: Notice: onboarding Protean Data as downstream partner (Order Form amendment) — quick legal checklist

Hi Alec / Markus,

Thanks for the heads-up — reviewed the Protean DPA draft and vendor spreadsheet. High-level summary and required changes:

1) Data categories: the draft incorrectly lists "diagnostic metadata" as non-personal. We need explicit language treating any identifiers used for customer correlation as personal data when tied to a customer account.
2) Subprocessor cascade: add an explicit flow-down clause mirroring MSA §7.4 (Audit & Subproc Flowdown) so that Protean must obtain written consent before engaging any downstream subcontractor who will handle customer-specific logs.
3) Audit rights & evidence: Protean must accept annual third-party SOC2 Type II scope or provide equivalent evidence; for onboarding we can accept an ETA that they provide Type II within 90 days but must grant audit access in the interim (read-only console or dedicated logs export).
4) Deletion and retention: limit retention to 30 days by default; any extension must be approved in writing and logged.

Suggested next steps:
- Orbital: confirm whether Protean will manage encryption keys or if they will use Redwood-managed customer keys (bring-your-own-key impacts our orderform annex).
- Markus/Jordan: accept the attached redline as our starting text (markus_proposed_redline_msa.docx). If Orbital insists on Protean's draft, we will produce a redline of that document and track differences in DocuSign.

I can prepare a concise DPA Annex template (Annex A: Subprocessor Obligations) that we prefer; if Orbital accepts we can attach it as an OF amendment rather than reworking the whole MSA.

Drive checklist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-legal-checklist

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
